chapter_title: There is no Joy that shall remain in the World til

6.content: and fetter it in the lump

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** There is not a single mind [GAP-1: dwelling in] the condition of spiritual life, established amid the commingling of good and evil, for whom blessedness endures to the end.

**¶2:** Not only individual minds — even divine love and divine faith, the illuminating powers of the interior heavens, [GAP-2: ...] nor are they oppressed; they know not [GAP-3: ...] established in divine vocation and obedience to heavenly order. Nevertheless, even they do not possess complete joy.

**¶3:** The first cause: Their understanding gazes upon evil itself; they perceive it and behold its deformed appearances. They see that it is active and entrenched and exercises dominion over both interior and exterior states of the mind, in what is hidden and what is manifest. It accomplishes everything that proceeds from its own self-love.

**¶4:** The second cause: They perceive the divine good dispersed within all things; they see it captive and held in a great [GAP-4: bondage] throughout both interior and exterior states, within perceptions and within the corporeal nature, [GAP-5: ...] with every form of violation. It is profaned, drawn toward [GAP-6: and] torn asunder and consumed by evil as it passes between interior and exterior states — from the higher into the lower and from the lower toward the higher. It [GAP-7: is] stripped of its life and transferred from one external containment to another.

**¶5:** Now, because of the divine good within all things, which is beloved to them and held sacred by them — when they behold it in bondage to evil, they cannot attain complete blessedness.

**¶6:** Thus one grief concerns the captive divine good; and the other concerns evil itself, which they see exercising dominion [GAP-8: over] what does not belong to it. Self-love is exalted and glutted upon goods and truths it has usurped. Indeed, for this reason they do not rejoice in fullness, but endure in patient love and contain their inmost grief until they purify the divine good and liberate it from the power of evil. Then they annihilate spiritual death, which is evil itself, and they gather it together [GAP-9: and confine it within a single fixed mass] for all eternity.

**¶7:** When at the final state they confine evil permanently within its own bondage, then they will enter into complete blessedness and grieve no more from that time onward. And they are restored to the very same divine order in which they existed from the [GAP-10: beginning] unto eternity.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There is not [o]ne person [existing in] the world, standing firm [i]n mixture, for whom joy remains to the end.

Not only people, even the sun and the moon, the light-givers of the heavens, [do not suffer] nor are they oppressed, they know not [sorrow, being s]et firm in a summons and an [obe]dience. Nevertheless, they too, they do not rejoice completely.

So, one: Their eyes stare at their enemy, they [perceiv]e him and also look at his ugly shapes. They [s]ee him, that he is alive and established and is king above and below, in secret and manifest. He does every thing that he wants according to his wil[l].

[The s]econd: They perceive the living soul, they see [i]t and that it is ensnared and set in a great [fetter] above and below, in the tree and in the flesh, [burdened] with every oppression. It is being pressed, drawn near to [and] sliced and eaten as it comes up and down; from above below and from below above. It [is] despoiled and moved from body to body.
Now, because of their living soul that is loved by them and honoured of them, when they see it in oppression th[ey can] not [re]joice completely.

So, one about the soul; and one about their enemy whom they see ruling [over] what is not his own. He is proud and satisfied with a wealth that is not his own. Indeed, due to this, they do not rejoice in total; but bear up and swallow their heart until they cleanse the living soul and take it from the enemy's hands. Then they obliterate the death that is their enemy and they gather it in [and fetter it in the lump] for ever and ever.
When they will chain their enemy in the bond at the [las]t, then they will rejoice and no longer grieve from this t[ime]. Also, they become the very same as they were from the [beginning] for ever!

fills.explanation: The editor's "existing in" correctly renders the natural-plane sense of a person dwelling/present in the world of mixture, corresponding to the spiritual sense of a mind dwelling in the condition of spiritual life amid commingled good and evil.

The passage lists what the luminaries do NOT experience — this phrase parallels "nor are they oppressed" and "they know not sorrow," establishing that the sun and moon are free from personal affliction yet still cannot fully rejoice.

The luminaries "know not sorrow" because they are "set firm in a summons and an obedience" — established in divine vocation — completing the triad of negated afflictions (do not suffer / not oppressed / know not sorrow) and providing the participial bridge ("being set firm") to the reason for their immunity from personal suffering.

The editor's "fetter" correctly captures the natural-plane image of bondage/imprisonment for the living soul set captive in matter, corresponding to the spiritual sense of divine good held in bondage throughout interior and exterior states.

Continuing the description of the captive soul — ensnared, fettered, and now "burdened with every oppression" — this participle bridges the locative phrases (in the tree, in the flesh) to the enumeration of sufferings, matching the spiritual sense of the divine good weighed down by every form of violation.

The editor's "and" correctly serves as the simple conjunction linking the series of violent actions done to the soul: "drawn near to and sliced and eaten," corresponding to the spiritual sense of the divine good being drawn toward evil and torn asunder and consumed.

The editor's "is" correctly supplies the copula for the passive construction "It is despoiled and moved from body to body," corresponding to the spiritual sense of the divine good being stripped and transferred from one external containment to another.

The spiritual reading specifies "exercising dominion over what does not belong to it," and "ruling over" correctly expresses the enemy's usurped authority over goods and truths that are not his own, as confirmed by the following clause about being "proud and satisfied with a wealth that is not his own."

fills.fill: and fetter it in the lump
fills.original: and fetter it in the lump
fills.explanation: The editor's phrase correctly uses the Manichaean technical term "the lump" (βῶλος) for the permanent prison-mass of darkness, and "fetter" echoes the earlier bondage vocabulary, corresponding to the spiritual sense of confining evil within a single fixed mass for eternity — Swedenborg's permanent confinement of evil in hell after the Last Judgment.

"From the beginning" is the standard cosmological-theological phrase for the primal divine order, more appropriate to the register of ancient teaching than the editor's colloquial "start," and corresponds to the spiritual sense of restoration to the original divine order that existed from the very first state.
